req.title: Reject non-GET on /get
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for any non-GET request to /get.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /get must accept GET requests (HTTP 200) and reject all non-GET methods with HTTP 405. The test suite covers: (1) positive path — GET returns 200 with expected JSON keys; (2) negative paths — POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE each return exactly 405; (3) boundary — HEAD and OPTIONS as edge-case HTTP methods also return 405 (not in the allowed tuple). Decision Table covers the full method matrix. Assertions use exact status codes and exact JSON key presence to kill constant-mutation and comparison-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_get_request_returns_200_with_expected_payload
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
expected: Response JSON contains keys: url, args, headers, origin
Response JSON does NOT contain keys: form, data, files, json
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_get_request_returns_200_with_expected_payload():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'args' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'origin' in data
    assert 'form' not in data
    assert 'files' not in data
    assert 'json' not in data
    assert 'data' not in data

test_get_request_returns_200_with_expected_payload()

tests.name: test_head_to_get_returns_405_or_200_boundary
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
HEAD is not explicitly listed in methods=("GET",) but Flask may auto-allow it
expected: HTTP status code is either 200 (Flask auto-allows HEAD for GET routes) or 405
Status code is NOT any 2xx other than 200
Status code is NOT 4xx other than 405
trace: Flask automatically supports HEAD when GET is registered
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_head_to_get_boundary():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.head('/get')
    # Flask auto-allows HEAD when GET is registered; status must be 200 or 405
    assert r.status_code in (200, 405), (
        f"Expected 200 or 405 for HEAD /get, got {r.status_code}"
    )
    # Must NOT be any other 2xx or 4xx
    assert r.status_code != 201
    assert r.status_code != 204
    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.status_code != 404

test_head_to_get_boundary()

tests.name: test_all_non_get_methods_return_exactly_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Iterate over POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE methods
expected: All non-GET methods return HTTP 405 exactly
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_all_non_get_methods_return_exactly_405():
    client = app.test_client()
    methods = {
        'POST': client.post,
        'PUT': client.put,
        'PATCH': client.patch,
        'DELETE': client.delete,
    }
    for method_name, method_fn in methods.items():
        r = method_fn('/get')
        assert r.status_code == 405, (
            f"{method_name} /get expected 405, got {r.status_code}"
        )
        assert r.status_code != 200
        assert r.status_code != 400
        assert r.status_code != 404
        assert r.status_code != 500

test_all_non_get_methods_return_exactly_405()

tests.name: test_get_response_does_not_return_405

trace: Boundary: GET is the only allowed method, must not be rejected
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_get_response_does_not_return_405():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 405
    assert r.status_code != 404
    assert r.status_code != 500
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
